purpose: Test whether increasing hidden width reduces full NVIDIA mHC training-time overhead between approximately 1B and 2B parameters
authorization: User requested larger-model measurement, then explicitly narrowed it to start at 1B and go to 2B

fixed.dataset: Existing frozen FineWeb-Edu sample-10BT packed rows, RustBPE32K
fixed.optimizer: Unchanged native MuonAdamW with existing batch/width LR and weight-decay scaling
fixed.arithmetic: BF16 backbone; PyTorch TF32 disabled; NVIDIA custom operators keep native precision; baseline NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0 and mHC unset, matching previous full comparison

capacity.selection: Largest common microbatch with peak reserved <=90% device total and >=4GiB free after updates; same selection for every size and variant

measurement.order: First ascending widths, baseline then mHC; second descending widths, mHC then baseline
measurement.primary: Full optimizer-step wall time with original finite checks
measurement.secondary: Forward/backward and optimizer event intervals, CUDA kernel attribution, PyTorch peak allocated/reserved memory
measurement.interpretation: Events include host gaps; profiler kernel times are attribution, not production wall time. Report forward/backward overhead separately so Muon cost cannot silently dilute total overhead.

gate: 9 new-width FP64 pipeline/head and real-2K causality/CCE/all-gradient checks; previously audited operators unchanged
limitations: Throughput diagnostics, not a quality comparison
Width scaling at fixed depth; does not separately test depth scaling
Previous 59M result has a different depth and potentially different GPU/microbatch; do not treat it as a matched point
No statistical population claim from two repeats on one GPU
